lessons.title: Limits, one-sided behavior, and continuity
lessons.objective: Evaluate elementary limits, compare one-sided behavior, and distinguish a nearby limit from a function value and continuity.
scope: Polynomial substitution where continuous; removable rational and radical forms
Two-sided finite limits require agreement of both sides
Continuity requires a defined value matching the limit
Signed infinite behavior describes unboundedness, not a real function value
Standard sine limit uses radians; finite tables suggest rather than prove limits
workedExamples: Polynomial limit at a negative input
Cancel (x²-9)/(x-3) for x≠3; limit6 while original value undefined
Rationalize (sqrt(x+4)-2)/x to obtain1/4
Left and right affine branches disagree at a junction
Repair a single point without changing its limit
Opposite signs for 1/(x-2) and matching positive infinity for its square
sin(3x)/x tends to3 in radians
lessons.guided: Separate the removable limit, assigned point value, and continuity for a factored quotient.

interaction.purpose: Change a junction, left/right approach values, and the isolated point. Predict existence and continuity, then reveal exact nearby values and a plot. Changing only the point must leave the limit unchanged.

mistakes: Substitute into 0/0 and stop
Treating an indeterminate form as an answer
Compare equivalent formulas only off the excluded point, then take the limit.
Use the plotted dot as the limit
Confusing nearby behavior with point evaluation
Compare left and right approaches independently of the assigned value.
Write infinity as an ordinary number
Extending real arithmetic without justification
Classify unbounded direction; no finite two-sided limit exists.
lessons.acceptance: Four checkpoints cover canceled-domain limits, radical and radian limits, one-sided/point continuity, and signs at poles.

lessons.title: Derivative meaning, polynomial rules, and rates
lessons.objective: Connect secants to instantaneous derivatives, differentiate polynomials, construct tangent lines, and interpret first and second derivatives with units and nondifferentiable corners.
scope: Difference quotient h≠0 and its h→0 limit
Power, constant, sum rules for polynomials
Tangent line y=f(a)+f′(a)(x-a)
Differentiability implies continuity; continuity alone is insufficient
Position, velocity, acceleration and their units; f′(a)=0 is local information
workedExamples: Expand the quotient for x²-3x, then let h approach0
Differentiate 2x³-5x+7
Tangent to x² at x=-1 is -2x-1
Derivative of |x-2| has left slope-1 and right slope1
Position 2t³-3t² gives velocity6t²-6t and acceleration12t-6
A horizontal tangent at one point does not make x² constant
lessons.guided: Compute the secant at a nonzero increment, its limit, and the resulting tangent line.

interaction.purpose: Change a quadratic, base point, and signed nonzero increment. Predict finite secant and limiting tangent slopes; reveal paired lines and a slope table. Reject h=0 in the original quotient.

mistakes: Set h=0 before simplification
Ignoring the original division
Use nonzero h, simplify, then take a limit.
Differentiate a constant to itself
Confusing value and change
A constant contributes zero rate.
Treat every continuous point as smooth
Ignoring one-sided slopes
A corner can be continuous with unequal limiting slopes.
Confuse velocity and speed
Dropping signs or units
Velocity is signed position change per time; acceleration is velocity change per time.
lessons.acceptance: Checkpoint includes exact derivative polynomials, secant/tangent distinction, corners, and signed velocity/acceleration with units.

lessons.title: Product, quotient, chain, and elementary rules
lessons.objective: Apply product, quotient, and chain rules, including elementary trigonometric, exponential, logarithmic, reciprocal, and root derivatives on valid domains.
scope: Differentiate products by two terms and quotients with squared denominator
Chain rule multiplies by inner derivative
Radian sine/cosine, e^u, ln(u) with positive u
Negative powers and square roots; derivative interior restrictions
Use existing polynomial inputs and exact derivative values or formula choices for nonpolynomial functions
workedExamples: (x²+1)(3x-2) differentiated with two product terms
(2x+1)/(x-3) derivative -7/(x-3)², x≠3
(2x-1)³ derivative6(2x-1)²
sin(4x) and cos(3x) with radian arguments
e^(-2x) derivative -2e^(-2x)
ln(3x+1) derivative3/(3x+1) on x>-1/3
(x+2)^(-2) and sqrt(2x+3), including boundary restrictions
lessons.guided: Identify inner and outer derivatives before evaluating a composite at a specified point.

interaction.purpose: Change a signed inner slope, intercept, and outer power. Predict outer derivative, inner derivative, and their product at a point; reveal a composition table and a local change comparison.

mistakes: Multiply derivatives of factors
Overgeneralizing the sum rule
Use u′v+uv′ and retain each undifferentiated factor.
Omit the inner derivative
Recognizing only the outer pattern
Track the change of the inner input as a second factor.
Use degree-mode trig derivatives
Forgetting argument units
Standard sine/cosine derivative rules use radians.
Ignore logarithm or root domain
Formal rules without conditions
Check the original expression and derivative denominator before evaluating.
lessons.acceptance: Independent work covers product/quotient structure, polynomial chain rule, all four elementary functions and nonpolynomial domain boundaries.

lessons.title: Integrals, signed accumulation, and the fundamental theorem
lessons.objective: Evaluate definite polynomial integrals, distinguish signed accumulation from total area or distance, and use the fundamental theorem with variable bounds and average values.
scope: Riemann sums as height times width and limiting accumulation
Polynomial antiderivative evaluation F(b)-F(a)
Reversed/equal bounds and signed area
Piecewise constant velocity: displacement versus total distance
Average value integral/(b-a), b>a
FTC with continuous integrand and a differentiable moving upper bound
workedExamples: Right rectangle sum for f(x)=x on[0,2] with four pieces is2.5 versus exact2
Integral of3x²-2 from0to2 is4
Integral of x from-1to1 is0 while geometric area is1
Velocity3m/s for2s then-2m/s for3s gives displacement0m and distance12m
Reverse bounds negate an integral; equal bounds give0
Average of x² on[0,3] is3
Derivative of integral from0to x² of(1+t²)dt is2x(1+x⁴)
lessons.guided: Evaluate a signed integral, reverse its bounds, and distinguish its average from an endpoint value.

interaction.purpose: Change two signed constant rates and interval widths. Predict signed accumulation, absolute accumulation, and average rate; reveal rectangles and a running-total table. Test cancellation without losing total distance.

mistakes: Make every integral positive
Confusing signed accumulation and geometric area
Keep signs for net change; integrate absolute values for total amount.
Subtract endpoints of f
Confusing integrand with antiderivative
Differentiate your candidate F before computing F(b)-F(a).
Forget upper-bound derivative
Treating a composite bound as x
Apply FTC first, then the chain rule.
Average endpoints automatically
Assuming a linear graph
Average value is total accumulation divided by interval length.
lessons.acceptance: Independent questions cover exact integration, bound orientation, signed and absolute motion/area, average value, and moving-bound chain factors.

lessons.title: Antiderivatives, substitution, and initial conditions
lessons.objective: Recover antiderivatives with constants, reverse simple chain rules, and use one or two initial conditions to select and verify a particular function.
scope: Indefinite integrals describe families differing by constants on an interval
Polynomial power rule except exponent-1; ln|x| on intervals avoiding0
Simple linear and quadratic inner substitutions including changed definite bounds
Elementary exponential/trig antiderivatives and inverse chain factors
One initial condition for first derivative; two for second derivative
Verify both the derivative relationship and every supplied condition; no general ODE methods
workedExamples: Antiderivative of6x²-4x is2x³-2x²+C
Integral1/x is ln|x|+C separately on positive/negative intervals
Integral(3x+1)² dx=(3x+1)³/9+C
Integral2x(x²+1)² dx=(x²+1)³/3+C
Integral2x(x²+1) from0to2 uses u1to5 and equals12
Integral e^(2x) is e^(2x)/2+C; integral cos(3x) is sin(3x)/3+C
y′=4x-3 and y(2)=5 gives y=2x²-3x+3
lessons.guided: Recover a polynomial from its derivative and an initial value, then verify both conditions.

interaction.purpose: Change a derivative and an initial point/value. Predict the required constant and a second function value, then reveal a family of vertically shifted curves. Explain why slopes alone cannot recover the starting value.

mistakes: Drop C
Treating a family as one curve
Differentiation loses constant offsets; initial information restores them.
Use power rule at n=-1
Dividing by a zero new exponent
Use ln|x| on a connected interval excluding zero.
Forget inverse chain factor or mix bounds
Incomplete change of variable
Transform the differential and bounds together or return fully to x before evaluation.
Use one constant after two integrations
Losing independent starting conditions
Each integration introduces a constant; verify all supplied conditions.
lessons.acceptance: Checkpoints cover family/elementary rules, substitutions and transformed bounds, a nonzero initial point, and two independent initial conditions.
